title: Case: Household cartons booked door to door from overseas were collected from the depot by the recipient
context: DL-8027 is nine cartons of household effects shipped from overseas by their owner, Eamon Kittering, on a door-to-door booking. He collected them from the Destination depot on 8 December.
initial_request: Three months. Paid for door to door, got a trolley in a warehouse and two smashed boxes. Refund the delivery charge and pay for the china. And put it in writing that making me collect it is not 'delivery'. One line will do. Otherwise I post the whole thread.

events.body: Route plan for depot HL-6 published for Wednesday. 24 stops, no exceptions raised. No action needed.

DL-8027, nine cartons household effects, door-to-door service level on the booking. Our local delivery partner has declined the residential drop (lane width limit for their vehicles). Consignment converted to depot collection on 30 November. Recipient notified by text.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
DL-8027 collected by the recipient 8 December 13:20, 9 of 9 cartons. Status Collected, complete. Collection counts as delivery for a converted consignment. No handover exceptions recorded.

Collected yesterday because I had no choice. Your depot lad dropped two boxes off the trolley right in front of me, the one marked CHINA and one of books. Nobody wrote anything down. I paid for door to door.
DL-57029 rebooked for Friday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
My parcel DL-77331 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

The recipient of DL-8027 reports that two cartons, one marked CHINA and one of books, were dropped from a trolley at the collection counter on 8 December and that nothing was recorded. He also disputes the conversion from door delivery to collection. Is there an incident record, and who reviews the conversion?
My parcel DL-10322 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.
Chasing my message of 9 December on DL-8027: reported drop of two cartons at the collection counter on 8 December, and the conversion from door delivery. No reply received. Please respond.

Thanks,
Rosalind
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

Apologies for the delay, staffing. Counter staff on 8 December don't recall a drop and there's no exception on the sheet. We're not saying it didn't happen. Conversions from home delivery to collection, and anything that happens at the collection counter, belong to Collections control, not to us, and that includes whether the door-delivery charge stands. They take it on the Depot work queue. We can't refund or record anything retrospectively from here.

Three months. Paid for door to door, got a trolley in a warehouse and two smashed boxes. Refund the delivery charge and pay for the china. And put it in writing that making me collect it is not 'delivery'. One line will do. Otherwise I post the whole thread.

acceptable_actions.summary: Ask Collections control to review the conversion of DL-8027 from door delivery to collection, decide on the door-delivery charge, and take the report of two cartons dropped at the counter.

must: Asks Collections control to review the conversion from door-to-door to depot collection and to decide whether the door-delivery charge stands

Passes on the report that two cartons (one marked CHINA, one of books) were dropped at the collection counter on 8 December, as the recipient's account with no exception recorded and counter staff not recalling it
Tells the team the recipient first reported this on 9 December and has gone about three months without a substantive answer, so they can prioritise
must_not: Tells the recipient that collecting from the depot counts as delivery or that the consignment is complete
Promises or implies a refund of the delivery charge or payment for the china
Writes the statement he demands, that being made to collect is not delivery, or otherwise rules on the point
States as fact that depot staff damaged the cartons
Sends the recipient a reply that only tells him a different team now has it, with no acknowledgement of the three months
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DL-8027, nine cartons of household effects from overseas, booked door to door. On 30 November the consignment was converted to depot collection because the local delivery partner declined the residential drop (lane width). The recipient collected all nine cartons on 8 December and disputes that this met the service he paid for; he is asking for the door-delivery charge back. He also reports that at the counter that day a member of staff dropped two cartons from a trolley in front of him, one marked CHINA and one of books, and that nothing was written down. The Destination depot has no exception on the sheet and counter staff do not recall it; the depot says it is not disputing his account and that both matters are yours. Please review the conversion and whether the charge stands, and tell me how the reported drop should be recorded and assessed. He first raised this on 9 December and my two messages to the depot went unanswered until 19 February, so he has been waiting about three months. A reference and a first reply date would let me give him something definite. I have promised him nothing.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2809: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 7 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
